fatal_errors: The proposed HEA coating is unrelated to the target intervention of liquid-metal dealloying a directionally segregated WTaVTi precursor in molten Cu to form aligned, bicontinuous Cu channels.
None of the cited evidence demonstrates that a W–Ta–Cr–V–Hf interlayer at a W/Cu interface lowers thermal boundary resistance or increases bulk W–Cu thermal conductivity.
The claimed phonon-matching mechanism and predicted 10–20% conductivity gain are asserted without direct calculations, interface measurements, or relevant prior experimental evidence.

The response generalizes irradiation resistance to fusion-relevant neutron or ion environments, whereas the relevant evidence and target are limited to specific low-energy ion or helium-implantation tests.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad goal and specifies a single intervention, control, measurable outcomes, and a usable falsification threshold. It is nevertheless not a reconstruction of the target study, which used 1200 °C/96 h liquid-metal dealloying to selectively replace Ti/V-rich channels with Cu while retaining a continuous WTaVTi RHEA network and a spontaneous W-rich interface. The proposed coating architecture, composition, processing route, and graded-interface mechanism all differ. E1–E3 support thermal stability and ion-irradiation tolerance of W–Ta–Cr–V–Hf films, but not their behavior as W/Cu interlayers or their effect on thermal conductance. E4 concerns WC-particle reinforcement of an HEA and is not probative. Conditions and boundaries are too vague to establish coating thickness, consolidation route, temperature window, irradiation spectrum, dose, or acceptable durability. The comparative experiment is reasonably discriminating, but the central thermal-conductivity claim remains unsupported.
